note: Instructions, instrument citation and all 10 statements transcribed verbatim from the study's own CC BY S1 Appendix; '1.'..'10.' numbering and the '(Item N)' / '(reversed, Item N)' tags stripped; the appendix's parenthetical '(each item is 1=strongly agree, 5=strongly disagree; a=0.91, M=2.34, SD=0.83)' dropped from instructions; the source's 'with the each of' kept as printed (not corrected). Item 6 and 8 line-wraps joined. Codes: data/enders_2022_conspiracy_vaccine.py keeps the Qualtrics column names VAXHES_1..10 (live == Raw Data.csv cell for cell); the deposit has no question-text row or codebook, so nothing in the study's files ties code to wording. Mapping: the appendix labels each statement '(Item N)' and the article's Table 2 prints F1/F2 loadings and uniqueness for 'Vaccine Hesitancy Item 1..10'. Re-running that EFA (iterated principal factors, 2 factors, 21 items per Analyses.do line 525, vaxhes_5/9/10 reversed per lines 154-156; listwise n 2043) matches Table 2 row N to VAXHES_N for all 10 with max |diff| 0.0005-0.0027 against runner-up 0.016-0.070; eigenvalues 10.670/1.784 vs 10.682/1.775. The same EFA's COVID-conspiracy rows land on COVCONS_3,2,4,7,6,5, exactly the Table 1 '(Item N)' labels batch_569 pinned independently from % agree, so the paper's Item N labels are a consistent wording key across its tables. Independent corroboration: the appendix's reversed set {5,9,10} (= Analyses.do's reverse-coded vaxhes_5/9/10) is the negatively correlated class (mean r with positive items -0.35/-0.34/-0.42 vs +0.61..+0.69); the two CDC statements (4, 6) are the two positive items most correlated with trust in public health officials (TRUST_PHO r .54, .63; others .44-.48). SOURCE OVERRIDE (response direction): the appendix prints '1=strongly agree, 5=strongly disagree' but the stored data run 1=strongly disagree .. 5=strongly agree, and the options are shipped that way. Evidence: positive statements are 57-74% at resp 4-5 (e.g. 'Vaccines are effective' 73.0%); they correlate +0.44..+0.52 with COVVAX (1 = vaccinated/will vaccinate, Analyses.do line 115; 1406 of 2055), reversed ones -0.28..-0.39; Analyses.do builds vaxhes = 6 - mean(items with 5/9/10 reversed) and the article says higher = more hesitant, which holds only if 5 = agree; Table 2's VHS loadings are negative where conspiracy-belief loadings are positive. Published scale M 2.34/SD 0.83/alpha 0.91 reproduced (2.3/0.83/0.91, n 2046) -- this fixes scale identity, not direction. Only endpoints labelled in the source; resp 2-4 option_text blank. Data stored raw (reversed items not recoded). Rights: VHS (Shapiro et al. 2018, Vaccine, Elsevier; from the WHO SAGE Working Group scale), here in the study's adult/US-CDC adaptation printed in its CC BY appendix; no instrument_rights_register.csv row; searched 2026-09-27 for VHS terms of use and found no fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause to quote, so extracted normally (silence, not a positive grant); no register row written.
